bull_bear.body: Dividend payout of ₹12/share (₹1,200cr total); ₹420cr capex; ₹100cr for potential M&A; net cash position maintained
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Input cost volatility (TiO2, resins); rural consumption slowdown; competitive pricing from Asian Paints and Berger; regulatory scrutiny on VOC emissions
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and optimistic; emphasized execution on rural penetration and sustainability; acknowledged cost pressures but highlighted pricing power and operational efficiency
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Rural demand surge is not just seasonal — repeat purchase rate up 31% YoY, indicating brand loyalty shift from unorganized sector
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- **Debt-free (D/E 0.03), net cash** — cash-deployment question repeatedly raised; management leaning to disproportionate reinvestment for growth over conservatism.
- **Dividend Rs 206/share FY26** (Rs 156 interim + Rs 50 final); no bonus; a share-split was requested by shareholders (no commitment).
- ICI India R&T rights issue subscribed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation (AGM 26)

bull_bear.body: Confident, ambition-forward. Chairman Parth Jindal framed FY26 as foundational and set unusually explicit market-position ambitions (#2 paints, #1 industrial, top-2 auto/specialty by 2031). CEO Rajiv Rajgopal candid that price hikes haven't fully offset crude. Governance solid: 50% independent board, 100%-independent audit committee, clean auditor's report. AGM was heavily retail-shareholder-driven (many Kolkata holders lobbying to keep the registered office in Kolkata); several detailed technical questions deferred to written replies.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone (AGM 26)

bull_bear.body:
- Distribution reach of 22,000+ dealers and presence in over 5,000 towns, targeted to expand to over 6,000 towns
- Legacy Dulux brand equity backed by a 10-year Dulux Assurance warranty programme, reinforcing premium positioning and consumer trust
- Access to JSW Group scale, combined manufacturing capacity across multiple locations, and cross-group institutional relationships (e.g. exclusive supply partnerships with JSW MG Motor India) following the 61.2% stake acquisition by JSW Paints
- Long-standing technical/strategic relationships in Industrial Paints, including a strategic partnership with the Indian Navy for high-specification anti-corrosive and anti-fouling coatings
- Exclusive supplier relationships in Automotive Plastic/Interior coatings (e.g. expanded exclusive partnership with Mahindra for Auto Interiors; exclusive supplier of automotive interior coatings for premium EV models)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Transition risk from integration with JSW Group — The ongoing transition of JSW Dulux into the JSW Group creates customer-continuity concerns around product quality, warranties, formulations and global technology access, and operational/IT transition activities (including phased ERP/applications migration) may create temporary business disruption if not tightly controlled.
- Geopolitical and raw-material sourcing volatility — Global geopolitical uncertainties are causing price fluctuations, availability challenges and longer lead times for several imported materials, which can lead to cost escalation, margin pressure and potential delays in production planning/stock coverage.
- Stakeholder retention during restructuring — The Company is encountering challenges in both retaining and attracting customers, vendors and employees amid the strategic transition, requiring active relationship-strengthening measures across all three groups.
- Occupational hazard in manufacturing — Manufacturing processes carry inherent risks of injury and occupational hazards from exposure to harmful materials/waste, mitigated through the Company's HSES policy, training and periodic risk assessments.
- Security, cyber and information control systems — Insufficient information security/cybersecurity systems — driven by end-user awareness gaps, tooling limitations and increasingly sophisticated attackers — pose risk of loss of sensitive information, intellectual property, banking data, business disruption and reputational damage; this extends to data-privacy compliance risk more broadly.
- Statutory compliance burden — A continually evolving local regulatory environment is increasing regulatory scrutiny and stakeholder compliance expectations; non-compliance poses a threat to the Company's financial and reputational standing.
- Talent attraction and retention — Market competition and a fast-evolving business environment create challenges in attracting and retaining talent, addressed through focused acquisition strategy, retention rewards and employee engagement.
- Loss of market share to competition — Intensifying competition and new entrants, including digital disruption, risk eroding market share in certain segments; mitigation centres on dealer-profitability competitiveness, brand investment and expanding numeric/geographic reach.

business.body:
- Deck's at-a-glance slide claims market share of 5% in Decorative Paints and 7% in Industrial Paints, and describes the company as Leader in Premium portfolio with iconic brands (Dulux, Sikkens, Lesonal, International).
- Distribution reach: headquartered in Mumbai with presence across >5,000 towns, ~22,000 retailers and ~4,000 B2B customers; 1,387 employees.
- Now a JSW Group company (formerly Akzo Nobel India Limited); deck cites strong governance with balanced Board composition between JSW Group and Independent Directors, and notes JSW Paints is unlisted.
- Two-pillar structure: a Decorative Paints business (B2C) and an Industrial Paints business (B2B) serving infrastructure, power, coil and automotive OEM customers.
- The glance slide carries a #4 marker alongside the share figures, but the extract does not state what that #4 ranks, so the ranking claim is not asserted here.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Carve-out] The deck's like-for-like columns exclude a carved-out / AN-retained business, described as provisional, unaudited and based on Mgmt estimates — so the statutory and L2L prior-year bases differ materially and are not interchangeable.
- [Rename] The filing is signed for JSW Dulux Limited (Formerly Akzo Nobel India Limited), BSE scrip 500710 / NSE JSWDULUX.
- [Related entity] Deck attributes dividend income of 55.9 Cr in the quarter to ICI India Research and Technology Centre Private Limited, and separately notes interest on IT refund of 21.5 Cr — both non-operating items.
- [Group footnote] The JSW Group slides carry a footnote reading Further 4.5mtpa capacity in Joint Venture currently, growing to 16mtpa by FY32, with market caps as on 3rd June 2026; extraction loses which group entity that capacity belongs to, and it is not stated to be JSW Dulux capacity.
- [Macro backdrop] Deck frames the period as resilient growth amidst cost and currency volatilities — FY26 GDP growth intact, dip in consumer confidence, uptick in inflation with RBI target breached, and the rupee weighed down by FII outflows and crude.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company manufactures and supplies paints, varnishes, enamels and lacquers across decorative and industrial end-uses, sold through a distributor/dealer network reaching over 5,000 towns and 22,000+ dealers. Its industrial portfolio spans Marine & Protective Coatings (anti-corrosive/anti-fouling solutions for naval and maritime vessels, Oil & Gas, Power, Mining, Infrastructure and Wind Energy), Automotive & Specialty Coatings (Vehicle Refinish, Automotive Plastic Coatings, Specialty Coatings for OEM and Consumer Electronics) and Coil & Extrusion / Metal Packaging Coatings for building & construction, infrastructure, appliances and metal packaging.

- **Marine and Protective Coatings:** International (brand), Ceilcote 380, Enviroline 376F60, Intershield 300, Intersleek 731, Intersleek 1001
- **Automotive and Specialty Coatings:** Sikkens, Wanda
- **Coil and Packaging Coatings:** Coil & Extrusion Coatings, Metal Packaging Coatings

outlook.body: Expansion into Tier 3/4 cities; entry into eco-friendly water-based coatings; potential acquisition of regional paint players in East India
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- **Ambition: become the #2 player in Indian paints & coatings** overall (from #4 in decorative today) — "come into the top three and then into the top two in decorative."
- **Industrial: nothing short of #1** — "Nothing short of being the number one player in industrial will be acceptable."
- **Top-two player in automotive & specialty coatings by 2031** (only dated target).
- Industry took **10-12% price increases** to offset crude/RM inflation, done gradually — **not fully offsetting** yet; will keep passing through as crude softens (Middle-East de-escalation helping).
- No specific FY27 revenue-growth or EBITDA-margin targets (management explicitly avoided numbers; detailed strategy "in the annual report").
outlook.title: Guidance (strategic/aspirational — no quantified FY27 numbers given) (AGM 26)

outlook.body:
- Strengthening Dulux brand equity through deeper consumer engagement and differentiated brand experiences to reinforce premium positioning
- Driving innovation in premium and adjacent segments of Decorative Paints, leveraging consumer insights and design trends
- Executing meaningful distribution expansion in Decorative Paints through deeper dealer penetration, enhanced retail presence and stronger painter engagement
- Strengthening the projects/institutional-sales business through tailored offerings and engagement with architects, developers and institutional customers
- Building organisational capability, talent and leadership development to foster a high-performance culture
- In Automotive and Specialty Coatings: strengthen position in the premium value-added segment while expanding participation in the mid-market segment, and explore emerging mobility segments
- Expanding Automotive and Specialty Coatings into new segments such as commercial vehicles and paint consumables
- In Marine and Protective Coatings: strengthen market position through differentiated solutions and increased participation in the mid-tier product portfolio across infrastructure, marine and industrial applications
- In Coil and Packaging Coatings: grow the premium extrusion business, leverage JSW Group strength to build the coil coatings business, sharpen mid-market play, and rebuild the packaging coatings business
- Continued investment in R&D, product innovation and technical service capabilities to support long-term growth and foray into new segments
- Cross-manufacturing integration with JSW Paints beginning Phase 1 between the Gwalior site and JSW Paints' Vijayanagar site to enhance operational integration and service efficiency
- Strategic capacity expansion at the Bengaluru plant to support the Automotive Plastics Coatings business
- FY2026-27 priorities: strengthen product portfolio across Decorative and Industrial Paints, invest in brand building, expand distribution to over 6,000 towns, improve efficiencies and maintain strict cost discipline
- Capture synergies across procurement, manufacturing, supply chain optimisation, distribution and overhead efficiencies with the broader JSW ecosystem to improve operating leverage over time
- Company follows a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy of distributing profits to shareholders. In FY26 the Board approved an interim dividend of Rs 156 per equity share (funded from the net profits realised on the slump sale of the powder coatings and international research centre operations), paid in September 2025, and recommended a further final dividend of Rs 50 per equity share for shareholder confirmation at the 72nd AGM.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company operates five manufacturing facilities and, during FY26, initiated preparations for cross-manufacturing of products for the JSW group, with Phase 1 beginning between its Gwalior site and JSW Paints' Vijayanagar site to enhance operational integration and service efficiency. At the Gwalior site, productivity improvements raised In-Line Disperser (ILD) batches from 34 to 38 in a two-shift operation for two ILDs, and the Company is aiming for further capacity expansion there through the addition of two filling lines and associated equipment to support future demand growth. Separately, in the Automotive Plastics Coatings business, the Company is pursuing strategic capacity expansion initiatives including additional capex investments at its Bengaluru plant, alongside plans to widen the business into new segments such as commercial vehicles and paint consumables.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rapid urbanisation: urban population in India expected to touch 600 million by 2031, driving residential demand
- Government infrastructure push: sustained public-sector spending on roads, bridges and transport, supported by a record Budget capex outlay
- Real estate momentum: expansion of affordable housing and 'ready-to-move' homes, supported by PMAY
- Rising middle class: growing disposable income and aspiration for premium home finishes, with the Indian middle class now comprising 31% of the population
- Industrial growth: strong bounce-back in manufacturing, energy, auto production and metallurgy driving demand for high-performance industrial and protective coatings
- Shift towards sustainable products: growing environmental awareness, green building adoption and stricter emission norms accelerating demand for eco-friendly, low-VOC and water-based paints and coatings
- EV ecosystem growth: rising EV registrations and penetration driving demand for high-performance coatings in battery packs and mobility components
- Shorter repainting cycles: consumers increasingly inclined toward repainting services, shifting the industry toward a service-oriented ecosystem
- Modular furniture growth driving demand for sophisticated wood finish and adhesive products
- Decorative segment continues to lead the paints market (approximately 75% of total demand) while the industrial segment (approximately 25%) is driven by automotive recovery and energy/metallurgy demand
- Decorative Paints demand was muted with heightened competitive pressures in H1 FY26, followed by a strong recovery in H2 FY26
- Headwinds flagged: fluctuations in raw material prices, existing and emerging geopolitical situations, and stringent VOC-related environmental regulations
- Opportunities flagged: use of nanotechnology in paints/coatings and rising demand for eco-friendly paints expected to offer market growth opportunities
- Competitive intensity in decorative paints continues to rise as established players increase capex on dealer networks and manufacturing capabilities amid new entrants
- Vehicle Refinish Coatings secured 150+ new bodyshop wins in FY26 and received exclusive Porsche India network approval
- Established exclusive partnerships, most notably with JSW MG Motor India, positioning the Company as a primary supplier for next-generation mobility
- Strengthened the Automotive Plastics Coatings business with a leading Indian automotive OEM, driving multi-fold revenue growth in FY26 on products developed at the Bengaluru R&D facility
- Expanded exclusive partnership with Mahindra for Auto Interiors across new car models
